summary: A required header, library, metadata module, or build tool has no realized provider in the current environment.
mechanism: The build plan identified a dependency clue, but the selected system-package or source realization is absent, unavailable, or incomplete.
trigger_patterns: Could not find a package configuration file provided by
Program\(s\) \[.*\] not found or not executable
autoreconf:.*failed to run .*: No such file
Neither a subproject directory nor a .*\.wrap file was found
fatal error: .*: No such file or directory

actions.hint: Resolve the missing file, metadata module, or build tool to a verified Debian provider in the current suite before installing it.
If no compatible system provider exists, use a repository-supported source dependency realization.

non_solutions: Do not guess package names from project names.
Do not reinstall a package already recorded as installed.

summary: System package installation failed because the requested providers conflict or are unavailable in the selected Debian release.
mechanism: A package transaction can fail when multiple mutually exclusive providers are requested or when a package name does not exist in the selected suite.

actions.hint: Reduce the request to one verified provider per family and retry the normalized package transaction.
Use an evidence-backed source realization when no compatible Debian provider exists.
Switch only to an untried release whose package metadata satisfies the dependency constraint.

non_solutions: Do not repeat the same failed package set.
Do not mix providers from different Debian releases.

summary: A realized dependency is not visible through the build system's discovery paths.
mechanism: The dependency may already exist, but pkg-config, CMake, Meson, the compiler, or the linker is not searching the selected installation prefix.
trigger_patterns: fatal error: .*: No such file or directory

actions.hint: Expose the verified dependency prefix through the discovery variable used by the current build system.
Install a verified provider only when the dependency is not already realized.
Register an evidence-backed source dependency when system metadata cannot satisfy the requirement.

non_solutions: Do not add unrelated global include or library directories.
Do not install a second provider before checking the selected realization.

summary: The selected build entry expects a generated build input or generated source that is absent.
mechanism: Repository checkouts commonly require a documented bootstrap or generator step before configure or compilation can consume generated inputs.

actions.hint: Execute an already-discovered bootstrap or generator command from the current Build Plan.
Use a source realization only when the missing generated input belongs to a separately managed dependency.

non_solutions: Do not invent a generator command that is absent from repository evidence.
Do not edit generated output by hand.

summary: The compiler or build tool rejects a requested option, generator, policy, version, or interface.
mechanism: The selected build command targets a compiler or build-tool interface that is unavailable in the active toolchain version.

actions.hint: Adjust only the rejected compiler or build-tool configuration selected by the Matrix.

non_solutions: Do not switch Debian release before trying the evidence-backed configuration change.
Do not reinterpret the error as a missing package without provider evidence.

summary: The active build step cannot invoke a required executable because no provider is available in the environment.
mechanism: A build entry, bootstrap script, generator, or compiler wrapper names an executable that is absent before the requested operation can run.
trigger_patterns: autoreconf:.*failed to run .*: No such file
Program\(s\) \[.*\] not found or not executable

actions.hint: Resolve the executable to a verified provider in the current Debian suite.
Use a project-supported source realization only when no compatible system provider exists.

non_solutions: Do not treat the absent executable as a missing generated output.
Do not guess a package name from the executable name.
